text:
maria: Heads up — noticed a p99+ latency spike on canary after yesterday's merge (release/rc-3.9 -> main). Impacting batch workloads. ~2.3x P99 for short-seq requests. Anyone bisecting yet? :eyes:

jon: saw the alert. link to perf run: https://ci.redwood/inference/perf/18234 — compare canary vs baseline. Can reproduce locally on a small repro.

lee: quick read of the diff shows a kernel selector tweak and a batching heuristic change in the same PR (PR #4123). Kernel selector now prefers fused-attn kernel for seq_len<=128 when batch>8. Batching heuristic lowered max_batch_delay from 8ms -> 4ms. That combo smells like more frequent smaller batches but different kernel path.

ash: @maria can you paste the p99 numbers from the perf dashboard?

maria: baseline main p99=42ms, canary p99=98ms on the short-seq trace (avg tokens 25). Throughput roughly same. CPU on host not saturated.

ci-bot: perf-job 18234 finished. Summary:
```
scenario: short-seq-mlperf-like
baseline: p50=18ms p95=55ms p99=42ms
canary:  p50=20ms p95=62ms p99=98ms
kernel-path: baseline=fallback-attn canary=fused-attn (for many samples)
cache-hits: baseline=84% canary=79%
```

jon: cache-hits drop + kernel switch = plausible. If fused-attn increases per-token compute for cached prefixes it could amplify p99.

lee: I can try to reproduce with a focused run toggling the kernel selection flag. Two quick knobs: `--kernel-prefer=fused` and `--max-batch-delay=8` to revert batching.

ash: doing a local bisect now. Steps I'm running: 
```
git bisect start HEAD main~20
git bisect bad HEAD
git bisect good main~20
# run the perf harness (short-seq config) and mark good/bad
```
I'll post the commit that flips it.

ash: initial findings — marking commit 1a2b3c4 (the PR merge) as bad. Bisect points to commit 1f7e9a5 which is the kernel selector refactor (author: @lee).

lee: ack. That refactor moved kernel-decider to runtime while also changing the threshold logic (seq_len * batch_size heuristic). I have a hunch: when batch_delay lowered we get more mini-batches where seq_len*batch_size falls below threshold, so fused-attn gets chosen more often. Fused-attn maybe has higher overhead for small KV-cache sizes.

maria: can we test a matrix: (kernel=old/new) x (max_batch_delay=4/8) x (kv-prefetch=on/off)? If we can reproduce p99 jump with kernel toggled only, that isolates it.

jon: I ran that matrix on a small DO instance: results attached (excerpt):
```
config A (old-kernel, delay=8): p99=44ms cache=85%
config B (new-kernel, delay=8): p99=46ms cache=84%
config C (old-kernel, delay=4): p99=47ms cache=82%
config D (new-kernel, delay=4): p99=101ms cache=78%  <-- big jump
```

lee: that pretty clearly shows the interaction. New kernel + smaller batches => bad. Likely a microkernel path that under-performs on many small KV segments.

ash: workaround options: revert the batching delay change (quick config rollback on canary) or gate the kernel selector behind a runtime flag until we fix fused-attn perf for small-KV.

maria: rollout blocker? If we keep canary with the change prod could hit customers. I'd say block the rollout and revert the batching heuristic change for now.

jon: +1. I'll file a hotfix PR to restore `max_batch_delay=8ms` on canary and add an integration test that exercises small-batch short-seq workloads.

lee: I'll open an investigation ticket to micro-bench fused-attn with varying KV cache occupancy and small batch sizes. Might be a kernel implement bug or cache-line behavior.

ci-bot: created issue INF-987: "fused-attn latency regression for small-batch short-seq; kernel selector interaction" and hotfix PR #4180 created by jon.

maria: thanks all — canary rollback in progress. After rollback, let's re-run perf job 18234 baseline vs patched-canary and confirm p99 back to baseline before unblocking. :thumbsup:

ash: local bisect + matrix confirmed. I'll add the bisect notes + commands to the ticket.

lee: will start a microbench and get kernel tracing (perf, flame graphs) next. If anyone has specific traces to reproduce let me know.

maria: adding short-seq trace file to the ticket. Good job everyone.
